Unlike sibling methods like [Radiance Caching (Jarosz et al.)](8493-radiance-caching-jarosz-et-al.md) which model directional radiance distributions, or [Light Cache Rendering Pipeline](9159-light-cache-rendering-pipeline.md) which uses 3D Summed Area Tables for aggregate queries, standard illumination caching typically stores scalar irradiance values derived from isotropic scattering assumptions [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim states that standard illumination caching typically stores 'scalar irradiance values derived from isotropic scattering assumptions'. While Source [S1] confirms that the specific technique discussed (TBRayMarcher) uses an 'isotropic' scattering assumption to pre-compute an illumination cache, it does not explicitly state that the stored values are 'scalar irradiance'. Furthermore, Source [S2] describes a caching technique that computes and stores 'global illumination' (which typically includes directional information and is not necessarily scalar irradiance derived from isotropic assumptions) using path tracing. The claim generalizes 'standard illumination caching' as typically storing scalar irradiance based on isotropic assumptions, but the evidence shows at least one method (S2) storing global illumination without mentioning isotropic assumptions, and S1 only describes a specific plugin's implementation without defining the general standard. Therefore, the evidence does not fully support the generalization made in the claim.
